title: When Called, O Lord, to Mourn the Doom
description: When Called, O Lord, to Mourn the Doom in Tonic Solfa to SAVED BY GRACE, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 615 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “"Thy will be done."”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre Double (8.8.8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SAVED BY GRACE; any other Long Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: When called, O Lord, to mourn the doom Of one af-fec-tion held most dear, While o'er the clos-ing, si-lent tomb, The bleed-ing heart dis-tils the tear, Though love its tri-bute sure will pay, And ear-ly streams of so-lace shun, Still, still the hum-ble soul would say, In low-ly dust, "Thy will be done."

lines: When called, O Lord, to mourn the doom
Of one affection held most dear, —
While o'er the closing, silent tomb,
The bleeding heart distils the tear, —
Though love its tribute sure will pay,
And early streams of solace shun,
Still, still the humble soul would say,
In lowly dust, "Thy will be done."
Whate'er, O Lord, thou hast designed
To bring my soul to thee in trust,
For all thy dealings, Lord, are just, —
Take all, but grant, in goodness free,
That love which ne'er thy stroke should shun;
Support this heart and strengthen me
To say in faith, "Thy will be done."

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to SAVED BY GRACE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
